revenuecat_wiring_review.web_stub_correct: revenuecatProvider.web.js returns supported:false, empty prices, {status:'failed', reason:'unsupported-platform'} on purchase, [] on restore, null on getOwnedProductIds -> matches contract.
revenuecat_wiring_review.controller_gating: revenuecat.js init() and getOwnedProductIds() both early-return when Platform.OS!=='android' || IS_DEV. On web Platform.OS==='web' so both are guaranteed no-ops. setBillingProvider(RevenueCatProvider) is NEVER called on web -> billing.js's DEV simulator path stays authoritative.
revenuecat_wiring_review.app_js_placement: RevenueCat.init() + RevenueCat.getOwnedProductIds().then(...) are placed AFTER setState(loaded)/setReady(true)/SplashScreen.hideAsync() inside Persistence.loadAll().then callback. Ready state and splash-hide happen BEFORE the RevenueCat calls, so even if RevenueCat threw synchronously (it doesn't on web) the app would already be visible. The .then() callback guards owned==null which is exactly what the web stub returns -> no state mutation on web. Correct implementation.

critical_code_review_comments: RevenueCat.init() call site is not wrapped in try/catch. On Android release builds, if the native module fails to load for any reason, an uncaught throw would still fire AFTER setReady(true) so the app remains usable, but a defensive try/catch around both RevenueCat.init() and the .then() chain (mirroring the existing outer .catch on Persistence.loadAll) would be cheap insurance. Not blocking for this release.

RevenueCat.getOwnedProductIds() has no .catch handler. If the native provider rejects (transient RC outage), an UnhandledPromiseRejection could surface. Consider adding .catch(()=>{}) or returning null on error inside revenuecat.js's getOwnedProductIds.

In App.js's reconciliation setState callback (lines ~138-150), Persistence.setPurchased/setBundle/setEasyMode/setRemoveAds are called from inside a setState updater. React may invoke the updater more than once in Strict Mode / concurrent rendering, causing duplicate persistence writes. Consider hoisting the Persistence.set* calls out of the updater (compute purchasedPigeons/... from `s`, then setState + persist outside).
